title: Email security with Secure Email
blurb: Tune sender reputation, mail flow policies and content scanning on the Secure Email Gateway (ESA).
scenario: Phishing is the top threat at the company. The **Secure Email Gateway** (formerly ESA) sits in front of the mail server for **scor.lab**. Configure it to throttle or reject mail from poorly rated senders, scan inbound mail for spam, viruses and malicious files, and check sender authentication.
topology:
Internet senders ── [Secure Email Gateway] ── Exchange (scor.lab)
                     listener: IncomingMail (public)
objectives: Put the stages of the email pipeline in order
Map sender reputation scores to HAT actions
Turn on scanning engines in the inbound mail policy
Use SPF, DKIM and DMARC to spot spoofing

steps.title: The email pipeline
steps.learn: Mail is checked in stages. The cheapest checks run first, while the connection is still open, and the expensive content scanning runs last.
steps.task: Put the stages in the order a message passes through them.
steps.question: Order from connection to delivery.
items: Sender reputation (SBRS) check on the connecting IP
Host Access Table (HAT) applies the mail flow policy
Recipient Access Table (RAT) checks the recipient domain
Advanced Malware Protection (file reputation and sandboxing)
Content and outbreak filters, then delivery

steps.title: Sender groups by reputation
steps.learn: **SenderBase Reputation Scores** (SBRS, from Talos) run from −10 (worst) to +10 (best). The HAT puts senders into groups by score, and each group gets a **mail flow policy**: accept, throttle or block.
steps.task: Give each default sender group its usual mail flow policy.
steps.screen: Secure Email › Mail Policies › HAT Overview

steps.title: Inbound mail policy
steps.learn: The **incoming mail policy** decides which engines scan each message. Quarantine positive spam, and put suspected spam aside for review instead of deleting it.
steps.task: In the default incoming policy: anti-spam **on** with positive spam **quarantined**, anti-virus **on**, **AMP** file reputation and analysis **on**, and **graymail** detection **on**.
steps.screen: Secure Email › Mail Policies › Incoming Mail Policies › Default Policy

steps.title: Spot the spoof
steps.learn: **SPF** lists the servers allowed to send for a domain. **DKIM** signs the message so changes can be detected. **DMARC** tells receivers what to do when SPF or DKIM fails to line up with the visible From domain, and where to send reports.
steps.task: Match each record to what it does.

fields.label: SPF
options: Lists the IPs allowed to send for the domain
Signs messages with the domain's private key
Sets the policy (none, quarantine, reject) for failures
fields.answer: Lists the IPs allowed to send for the domain

fields.label: DKIM
options: Lists the IPs allowed to send for the domain
Signs messages with the domain's private key
Sets the policy (none, quarantine, reject) for failures
fields.answer: Signs messages with the domain's private key

fields.label: DMARC
options: Lists the IPs allowed to send for the domain
Signs messages with the domain's private key
Sets the policy (none, quarantine, reject) for failures
fields.answer: Sets the policy (none, quarantine, reject) for failures

steps.title: Retrospective verdicts
steps.question: An attachment was clean when it was delivered, but an hour later AMP rates it malicious. What can the gateway do?

options.text: Send a retrospective alert and, with Office 365 or Exchange integration, remediate the message in mailboxes (Mailbox Auto Remediation).
Nothing. Once a message is delivered, the gateway is done with it.
options.why: AMP keeps tracking file verdicts. Retrospection is one of its main features.

options.text: Recall the message from the sender's server.
options.why: The gateway acts on your own mailboxes, not the sender's.

summary: The email pipeline from reputation to delivery, HAT sender groups mapped to mail flow policies, an inbound policy with anti-spam, anti-virus, AMP and graymail, and SPF, DKIM and DMARC for spoofing.
